At the same time, the chipmaker said it will stop selling its H200 chips in China, and it dismissed calls to […]

articles.title: Signal bloquea capturas de pantalla y el acceso de Siri IA a la pantalla
articles.raw_content:
Signal is restricting the ability to take screenshots on Android and iOS devices in an effort to prevent AI agents from reading users' messages and other data. The agentic AI capabilities built into operating systems that analyze on-screen information to learn more about the user are "undermining Signal's ability to independently guarantee privacy," Signal president Meredith Whittaker said in a blog post, while urging OS providers to make it easier for app developers to control what data agents can access.

articles.title: Voyager 1 a un día luz: historiador revisita detalles olvidados del Golden Record
articles.raw_content:
In the one light-day that humanity's most distant object has now traveled from Earth, there has been enough time for details about its creation—and what it left behind—to be discovered again.

Voyager 1, which left Earth in 1977 on an initial mission to fly by Jupiter and Saturn (as well as the latter's moon Titan), crossed into interstellar space in 2012. Like its twin (Voyager 2), Voyager 1 carries a "commemorative phonograph record," in part as a nod to the 100th anniversary of the recording medium and as a message from humanity to whoever (or whatever) encounters the spacecraft on its journey through outer space.

About those forgotten bits, ask Glen Swanson. While researching the history of the Golden Record, he uncovered the discs' overlooked second set of operating directions and located the duplicates that were made and distributed almost five decades ago.

articles.summary: En el día luz que ha recorrido Voyager 1 desde su partida, el historiador Glen Swanson ha recuperado datos olvidados del Golden Record, como un segundo conjunto de instrucciones de operación y copias duplicadas de la década de 1970, revelando más sobre la misión y su mensaje a posibles receptores.

articles.title: Jensen Huang dispuesto a volver como CEO de Nvidia
articles.raw_content:
Jensen Huang, who resigned as Nvidia's CEO last week, would be willing to return as CEO if the company's board of directors wanted it, he said in a statement reported on by The Wall Street Journal.

"Since my departure, I've seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia's employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO," Huang said. "If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO."

Huang resigned on Thursday following reports of two affairs, including one with an alleged …

Read the full story at The Verge.
articles.summary: Jensen Huang, quien renunció la semana pasada, ha declarado que estaría dispuesto a regresar como director ejecutivo de Nvidia si la junta lo decide. El CEO ha recibido numerosas peticiones de empleados, inversores y socios. Su salida se produjo tras escándalos de relaciones personales. La decisión dependerá de los intereses de accionistas y la empresa.

articles.title: Ars Live: What do drone strikes on data centers mean para the
articles.raw_content:
Drone and missile strikes have inflicted unprecedented damage on data centers in Eastern Europe and the Middle East this year, disrupting cloud services for millions of people and permanently deleting some Amazon Web Services customer data. This trend represents a new concern for Big Tech companies—but also for governments and everyone else who depends on common digital services in modern life.

To explore what this all means for modern society’s reliance on cloud resilience, I will be hosting a live conversation titled "Drone attacks and data centers: New Risks for Big Tech" on Tuesday, November 17 at 1 pm ET with Joseph Jarnecki, a senior research fellow at the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI), a UK defense and security think tank. He leads RUSI’s work on how cloud services factor into national security and defense, along with tech sovereignty efforts.

Jarnecki has done extensive research on how Ukraine strengthened its cloud resilience with Western partners despite facing both cyberattacks and kinetic attacks at the start of the full-scale Russian invasion, and explored what that means for NATO and European governments’ cloud adoption plans.

articles.title: Aliados de Huang montan una sala de guerra para su retorno a Nvidia
articles.raw_content:
Jensen Huang is considering a comeback as Nvidia’s chief executive, as allies in Silicon Valley pressure the company’s board to reinstate him days after the tech executive resigned over reports he had affairs with a suspected Chinese spy and a subordinate.

Huang has discussed with confidants the possibility of returning, according to multiple people familiar with the matter—even as an independent probe by Nvidia’s board investigates the conduct that led to a spectacular leadership crisis at the $4 trillion chip company this week.

One Huang ally told the FT they were putting together a “war room” of Silicon Valley executives to lobby for the former Nvidia chief’s return and would try to garner support from the White House.
